key: If the age was unsuitable and their mission at failure, they fell back upon their own resources and waited.
s: The chapter denies that the retired scholars of old hid, blaming the times; Guo Xiang, on 16.27, reads the waiting as a sage’s calm in a busy age: rooted deep, he waits for things to act of themselves, so the Way is not lost.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 16, on 16.27, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 18, Zhengtong Daozang), revision 6365330 (2026)

evidence.words: 雖有事之世，而聖人未始不澹漠也，故深根寧極而待其自為耳，斯道之所以不喪也。
evidence.gloss: Even in an age given to affairs, the sage is never other than calm and still; so he roots himself deep, rests in the utmost, and waits for things to act of themselves; this is how the Way is not lost.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Zhuangzi 16.27, at 1447); the Chinese 不當時命而大窮乎天下，則深根寧極而待 is the line Giles renders. Read Guo Xiang on all of chapter 16: his note on 深根寧極而待 says the sage in an age of affairs is still calm, roots deep and waits for things to act of themselves, which is why the Way is not lost; the sentence carries exactly that and adds nothing. Plain sense faithful to 16.27 (the retired scholars of old did not hide themselves; the times were not suited to them). entry-check ok.
